mainTopic: A widow's מזונות after partial collection, the oath and announcement when she sells estate property, and the משנה on a widow who sells at the wrong price.
overview: The עמוד opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: how רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read the word 'בבתוליה'. That line shows their dispute is about reading a פסוק, not about whether part of the money counts like all of it. Next, a widow takes a silver cup toward her כתובה and still asks for food. רבא tells the יתומים to feed her, since no one disputes רבי שמעון that partial payment is not full payment. Then רבה בריה דרבא asks רב יוסף whether a widow who sells without בית דין must take a שבועה. He explains that he has no doubt about a הכרזה, because רב נחמן's ruling seems to show that a sale to others works without one. The גמרא pushes that proof aside with the idea 'Who appraised it for you?', backed by רבי אמי's case of the orphans' coral. The final הלכה is that she needs a שבועה but not a הכרזה. A new משנה follows about a widow who sells at the wrong price or sells more than her כתובה covers. The גמרא begins asking why she cannot keep the profit when she overcharges, and רב נחמן's answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Reading 'in her virginity' as all of her virginity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining how רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read 'בבתוליה': her virginity must be fully intact in every way. That is a matter of reading the פסוק, not the question of מקצת כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In her virginity' means all of her virginity must be intact, whether from natural or unnatural relations.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of an earlier back-and-forth. The גמרא explains the derivation of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון from the word 'בבתוליה', so their argument is about how to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone tried to link a dispute between תנאים about a כהן גדול marrying a בוגרת to the question of whether part of the money counts like all of it. This line finishes the rejection of that link: the extra letters in 'בבתוליה' teach that she must be a full בתולה in every way. So that dispute can't be used as a source for מקצת כסף.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In her virginity': a word from the פסוק about the wife of a כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument that started on the previous עמוד. Don't read it as a brand-new topic. It closes the attempt to tie the כהן גדול dispute to the question of part-payment.

phrases.english: "In her virginity"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:13, about the woman a כהן גדול may marry.

phrases.english: means that all of her virginity must be intact,
whether in the natural way or in an unnatural way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a discussion that began before this text, showing that the תנאים argue about reading a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying the תנאים's dispute about a בוגרת to the question of מקצת כסף ככל כסף.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their opinion comes from reading 'בבתוליה' as 'complete virginity in every way', not from a view about partial payment.

steps.title: A widow who took a silver cup still gets food
steps.stepSummary: A widow took a silver cup as part of her כתובה and also asked for food. רבא told the יתומים to feed her, because no one disagrees with רבי שמעון that part of the money is not like all of the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman grabbed a silver cup toward her כתובה and was still asking for food. She came to רבא. He told the orphans: Go give her food. No one is concerned about רבי שמעון's view that part of the money is not treated like all of the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. A widow already collected part of her כתובה, and רבא rules that she still gets מזונות from the יתומים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow gets מזונות from the estate until she collects her כתובה. Here she collected only part of it. רבא rules she is still fed, relying on רבי שמעון's rule that part of the money is not treated like all of it. Since no one disputes that rule, she has not yet been 'paid', and her food support continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Food support that a widow gets from the estate
There is no one who is concerned about (this opinion)
Part of the money counts like all of the money

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a widow who has collected only part of her כתובה still receives מזונות, following רבי שמעון that part of the money is not like all of the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling: grabbing part of the כתובה does not end the widow's right to be fed.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman who seized a silver cup
toward her כתובה, and she was demanding food.
phrases.notes: She took the cup on her own from her late husband's property, as part of what the כתובה owes her.

phrases.english: She came before רבא.
He said to the orphans:
Go give her food,
there is no one who is concerned about this view of רבי שמעון,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת כֶּסֶף כְּכׇל כֶּסֶף.
phrases.english: who said: we do not say that part of the money is like all of the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דִּתְפַסָה כָּסָא דְכַסְפָּא בִּכְתוּבְּתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of מקצת כסף to a real court case that involves it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow who seized part of her כתובה still receives מזונות from the יתומים, since no one disputes רבי שמעון that partial payment is not like full payment.

steps.title: Must a widow who sells outside court take an oath?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בריה דרבא asks רב יוסף whether a widow who sells her husband's property without בית דין must swear an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה son of רבא sent to רב יוסף: A widow who sells without בית דין: does she need an oath, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבה בריה דרבא wants to know if a widow who sells estate property on her own must take a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow may sell property from the estate to pay for her food or her כתובה. When she does it without בית דין, the question is whether she must swear that she did not take more than she was owed.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: רבה son of רבא sent to רב יוסף:
A widow who sells not in בית דין,
does she need an oath,
or does she not need an oath?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a widow selling estate property.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a widow who sells without בית דין must take a שבועה.

steps.title: Why not ask about a public announcement too?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף pushes back: you should also be asking whether she needs a הכרזה before the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you should ask about a public announcement!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers with a challenge. He says there is a bigger question to ask: must she announce the sale publicly? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הכרזה makes sure the property is sold for its true value. רב יוסף suggests that a sale without בית דין raises this question even before the question of an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: A public announcement before selling property
And you should be asking (as well)

phrases.english: And you should ask about a public announcement!
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף talking back to רבה: why aren't you also asking whether she has to announce the sale?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the question in step 3 was framed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בריה דרבא's choice to ask only about a שבועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a sale without בית דין is uncertain, the need for a הכרזה should be in doubt too, so why leave it out?

steps.title: No doubt about an announcement; only the oath is in question
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that he has no question about הכרזה. רב נחמן ruled that a widow who appraises the property for herself has done nothing, and step 6 shows how this implies that a sale to others needs no announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have no question about an announcement, because רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן: a widow who appraised the property for herself has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בריה דרבא answers רב יוסף. He shows that the need for a הכרזה is already settled, so his only question is about the שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ruled that a widow who sets the value herself and takes the property for herself has done nothing. רבה reads this as implying that selling to someone else does work, even without an announcement. So he sees no question about הכרזה, and only the oath is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it
She appraised, set a value on
She has done nothing at all: the action has no effect

steps.whatToRemember: רבה has no doubt about הכרזה: from רב נחמן's ruling, which cancels only an appraisal 'for herself', he infers that a sale to others needs no announcement. His only question is the שבועה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבה son of רבא answering רב יוסף.

phrases.english: About an announcement I have no question,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: because רבי זירא said that רב נחמן said:
A widow who appraised the property for herself
has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַכְרָזָה לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by showing that הכרזה is already settled.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no doubt about הכרזה, because רב נחמן's ruling implies that a sale to others is valid even without one. So only the שבועה is in question.

steps.title: Proving from רב נחמן that a sale to others needs no announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבה reasons that רב נחמן's case must be one with no הכרזה. So only a sale to herself fails, while a sale to someone else works even without an announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there was a public announcement, why would she have done nothing? So it must be that there was no announcement. It is only when she takes the property for herself that she has done nothing. If she sells to someone else, what she did stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why רבה had no question about הכרזה. It reads רב נחמן's ruling closely to show that a sale to someone else works even without an announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there had been a public announcement, she would be like any normal buyer, and her purchase should work. So רב נחמן must be talking about a case with no announcement. Since he only cancels a sale 'to herself', a sale to an outsider without an announcement must be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
They publicly announced the sale (from הַכְרָזָה)
She has done nothing; her act does not count at all

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He means: in רב נחמן's case, where the widow appraised the property for herself.

phrases.english: If they publicly announced it,
why has she done nothing?
Rather, is it not that they did not announce it,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְעַצְמָהּ הוּא דְּלֹא עָשְׂתָה וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: and it is only for herself that she has done nothing,
but to someone else,
what she did is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רב נחמן's ruling, quoted in step 5, shows that a הכרזה is not needed.
steps.raayaObject: A widow's sale to someone else is valid even without a הכרזה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling that a widow who appraises for herself has done nothing, read as a case with no announcement.

steps.title: There was an announcement, but no one appraised it for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רב נחמן's case could have had an announcement. Her act fails because nobody appraised the property for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, there was an announcement, and we say to her: Who appraised it for you?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 6. It explains רב נחמן's case another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on there being only one reason her purchase could fail: no announcement. The גמרא offers a second reason: even with an announcement, she set the price herself and no proper appraisal took place. Now רב נחמן's ruling says nothing about whether a sale to others needs a הכרזה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (used to keep the original case and explain it differently)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the announcement and the appraisal. The announcement tells the public about the sale. The appraisal is a proper outside estimate of the property's value. Here the first happened, but the second did not.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where they did announce it,
and where they say to her:
Who appraised it for you?
phrases.notes: He means nobody else set the price. She set it herself, so the deal doesn't count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 6 by giving another reading of רב נחמן's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not rule on whether a הכרזה is needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only possible flaw was a missing announcement. The flaw could instead be a missing appraisal.

steps.title: A man appraises orphans' coral for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story that matches the idea of 'Who appraised it for you?': a man appraised orphans' coral for himself at 400 זוז, and it rose to 600.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of a man who was given orphans' coral to watch. He appraised it for himself at four hundred זוז. It went up in value and was worth six hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story that shows the same problem as step 7. The question of who gets the profit comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the widow, this man set the price for himself, with no one else appraising it. The value then went up, so it matters whether he ever really bought it. If the sale counts, the extra 200 is his. If it does not, the profit belongs to the יתומים.

phrases.english: Like this case of a certain man
with whom they deposited coral belonging to orphans.
He went and appraised it for himself
at four hundred zuz.
It went up in value and stood at six hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that illustrates the 'Who appraised it for you?' idea from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of someone who appraises another's property for himself. The ruling follows in the next step.

steps.title: רבי אמי asks: Who appraised it for you?
steps.stepSummary: The man came to רבי אמי, who answered with the same words: 'Who appraised it for you?' A price he set for himself does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי אמי. רבי אמי said to him: Who appraised it for you?
steps.whatsHappening: The man asks רבי אמי who gets the profit. רבי אמי answers with the exact phrase from step 7, showing that an appraisal you make for yourself means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because no one else appraised the coral, he never bought it, and it still belonged to the יתומים. The words 'מאן שם לך' here match the words in step 7. This shows that the answer given for רב נחמן's case is a known idea and not something made up just to push aside the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל who rules on the case
Before him (came to him for a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: A person who sets the price of someone else's property for himself has not bought it. The phrase 'Who appraised it for you?' sums this up. Because of it, רב נחמן's ruling cannot prove that a widow's sale needs no הכרזה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a proper outside appraisal is a separate requirement from a public announcement. So רב נחמן's ruling no longer proves anything about הכרזה, and the next step gives the final ruling on it.

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Ammi.
He said to him: Who appraised it for you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אמי's ruling on the story set up in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rise in value belong to the man or to the orphans?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since no one appraised the coral for him, he never acquired it.

steps.title: Final ruling: an oath is needed, an announcement is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a widow selling property for her כתובה must take a שבועה but does not need a הכרזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the final law is: she needs to take an oath, but she does not need to make a public announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה that ends the discussion about how a widow sells property to collect her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate requirements were in play: a שבועה and a הכרזה. The ruling keeps the שבועה but drops the הכרזה. This fits רבה's view from earlier: a sale to someone else works even without an announcement.

keyTerms.meaning: A public announcement before a sale

steps.whatToRemember: A widow selling for her כתובה: שבועה yes, הכרזה no.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the whole discussion about how a widow collects her כתובה by selling property.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: she needs an oath,
phrases.notes: The oath is that she has not taken more than she is owed.

phrases.english: but she does not need a public announcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate about הכרזה and the story of רבי אמי with a final practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A widow selling for her כתובה must take a שבועה, but a הכרזה is not required.

steps.title: New משנה: a widow who sells at a bad or good price
steps.stepSummary: If her כתובה is 200 and she sells property for the wrong price, either too high or too low, her כתובה counts as fully paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A widow whose כתובה was 200, and she sold something worth 100 for 200, or something worth 200 for 100, has received her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that when the widow sells property for her 200 כתובה, a pricing mistake in either direction is her own concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case she gained: she got 200 for land worth only 100. In the second case she lost: she got only 100 for land worth 200. Either way, her כתובה is treated as fully collected, and she cannot claim anything more from the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: Her כתובה has been received in full

steps.confusionAlert: In the second case she received only 100 in cash. Even so, her כתובה counts as fully paid, because she sold land worth 200. The loss is her own.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A widow whose כתובה was two hundred,
and she sold something worth one hundred for two hundred,
or something worth two hundred for one hundred —
has received her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from how the widow sells to what happens when the price is wrong.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the widow sells property worth her full כתובה at a wrong price, her כתובה counts as collected.

steps.title: Selling even one דינר too much cancels the sale
steps.stepSummary: If her כתובה is 100 and she sells property worth 100 and one דינר, the sale is void, even if she offers to return the extra דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her כתובה was 100, and she sold something worth 100 and a דינר for 100, the sale is void. Even if she says, 'I will give the דינר back to the heirs,' the sale is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposite problem. Here she sold more property than her כתובה covered, and that cancels the whole sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her right to sell reaches only as far as her כתובה. The extra דינר's worth of land belonged to the orphans, so she sold something that was not hers to sell. Offering to repay the דינר does not fix the sale.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same as Step 11. There the property matched her כתובה and only the price was off. Here the property itself is worth more than her כתובה.

phrases.english: If her כתובה was one hundred,
and she sold something worth one hundred and a dinar for one hundred —
her sale is void.
Even if she says:
I will return the dinar to the heirs —
the sale is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מָנֶה, וּמָכְרָה שָׁוֶה מָנֶה וְדִינָר בְּמָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 11: this time the property sold is worth more than her כתובה, not just mispriced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling property worth even slightly more than her כתובה cancels the sale, and offering to return the extra does not help.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the sale stands unless the extra is a usable plot
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the sale is valid unless the extra land is a meaningful size: nine קבין in a field, half a קב in a garden, or a quarter קב according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The sale always stands, unless enough was left over that she could have kept back a piece of land: in a field, an area for sowing nine קבין; in a garden, half a קב; and according to רבי עקיבא, a quarter קב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says a small overage does not cancel the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion cancels the sale over even one דינר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל cancels it only if the extra land is big enough to be worth working on its own. Below that size, she just pays back the difference to the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: An area for sowing nine קבין of seed
An area for sowing a quarter קב of seed

steps.whatToRemember: Two views: the first opinion cancels the sale over even one extra דינר; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל cancels it only if the extra is a workable plot.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Actually, her sale stands,
unless there is enough there that she would have left over
in a field — an area for nine kav,
phrases.notes: A קב is a measure of seed. The size is how much land that amount of seed would sow.

phrases.english: and in a garden — an area for half a kav,
and according to Rabbi Akiva — an area for a quarter kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם מִכְרָהּ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 12's ruling that even one extra דינר cancels the sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sale stands unless the excess is a usable plot: nine קבין in a field, half a קב in a garden (a quarter קב according to רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: Several sales, and only the last one is underpriced
steps.stepSummary: The widow's כתובה is 400 זוז. She sells property in several sales of 100 each. The last property is worth 100 and one דינר but is sold for only 100. Only the last sale is void; all the earlier sales stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her כתובה was 400 זוז and she sold property to one person for 100, to another for 100, and to the last person she sold property worth 100 and a דינר for only 100, then the last sale is void, and all the other sales are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its final case. Here the widow collects her כתובה through several separate sales instead of one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sales were sold at the right price, so they are fine. Only the last sale was undercharged by a דינר. Like the case in Step 12, that one sale is void. A mistake in one sale does not cancel the good sales before it.

keyTerms.meaning: 400 זוז, the amount of her כתובה in this case
A coin value equal to 100 זוז
Void; the sale does not count

steps.whatToRemember: Each sale is judged on its own. One underpriced sale is void, but the correctly priced sales before it stay valid.

phrases.english: If her כתובה was four hundred זוז
and she sold to this one for a מנה,
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 זוז, so each of these sales covers a quarter of her כתובה.

phrases.english: and to that one for a מנה,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 12 (an overreach of one דינר voids the sale) to a case with several sales. Step 13 had added רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion; this case goes back to the main rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the widow makes several sales, only the sale that was underpriced is void, and the correctly priced sales remain valid.

steps.title: Why can't she keep the profit if she overcharged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rule from Step 11. If she undercharged, the heirs can tell her the loss is her own fault. So if she overcharged, she should be able to say the profit is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about property worth 200 sold for 100? There they tell her, 'You caused the loss.' Then for property worth 100 sold for 200, let her also say, 'I made the profit!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the משנה's rule from Step 11. That rule said that whether she sold too low or too high, her 200 כתובה counts as fully paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she undercharges, she has taken property worth her full כתובה, so the loss is her problem. By the same logic, when she overcharges, she has used up only 100 worth of property. She should then be allowed to keep the profit and still collect another 100. The גמרא wants to know why the two cases are not treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? The גמרא uses this to ask why two cases get the same (or a different) ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful about which case is which. 'Worth 200 for 100' means she undercharged, so she lost money. 'Worth 100 for 200' means she overcharged, so she gained money. The question is why both cases end with her כתובה counted as fully paid.

phrases.english: גמרא
What is different about property worth two hundred sold for a מנה,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the case in Step 11, where her כתובה was 200.

phrases.english: where they say to her: You caused the loss?
phrases.notes: The ones saying this are the husband's heirs.

phrases.english: Then for property worth a מנה sold for two hundred, also,
let her say: I made the profit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the משנה finished, the גמרא opens and goes back to challenge the first rule (Step 11).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule in Step 11 that an overpriced sale also counts as full payment of her כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'it's your own loss' reasoning used for underpricing should work the other way for overpricing: she should keep the profit and still collect the rest of her כתובה.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins his answer in the name of רבה בר אבוה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, begins to answer the question. His actual answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces who will answer. The גמרא is setting up the answer, and the content comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer quoted from an earlier teacher is coming. It will explain why the profit from an overpriced sale does not belong to the widow.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who quotes the answer
The teacher whose answer רב נחמן is quoting
